priorStories.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula advance to runoff
priorStories.body:
Brazil’s electoral court said Flávio Bolsonaro received 47.03% of valid votes and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva received 45.16%, with 99.99% of ballots counted.

Neither secured a majority, sending them to a presidential runoff on October 25.

priorStories.headline: Germany adds €1 billion in Ukraine military aid
priorStories.body:
Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced €1 billion in additional military aid for Ukraine and €350 million to repair its energy system during a visit to Kyiv.

German executives also signed 14 agreements with Ukrainian government and business counterparts worth about €6.6 billion. They include agreements involving IRIS-T missiles, radar equipment and interceptors for jet-powered drones. A broader defense-production agreement remains under negotiation.

priorStories.headline: Yemen’s government launches offensive against Houthis
priorStories.body:
The head of Yemen’s Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council announced military operations intended to retake Houthi-controlled territory and extend government authority nationwide.

Government-aligned forces said they were striking Houthi targets in Sanaa and Saada. Houthi-run media attributed an attack on Sanaa to Saudi Arabia, but Saudi officials had not confirmed that account. No territorial gains were reported in the initial accounts.

candidates.summary: The Nobel Assembly awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. Hegemann and Nagel discovered the light-sensitive protein channelrhodopsin, and Deisseroth developed its use as a light-controlled switch for nerve cells.
candidates.title: Optogenetics researchers win Nobel medicine prize

candidates.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced that an extraordinary cabinet meeting would be called to dissolve parliament and schedule a general election for November 29. Sánchez said a renewed mandate was needed after repeated parliamentary deadlock, including the rejection of government housing measures.
candidates.title: Spain calls early general election for November 29

candidates.summary: Norway’s government said it would submit legislation proposing a temporary ban on AI-equipped glasses in selected public and privacy-sensitive locations. Possible locations include schools, parks, museums, public events, medical facilities and changing rooms. The proposal is not yet law, and the government said private use and some other uses would remain permitted.
candidates.title: Norway proposes temporary restrictions on AI glasses

candidates.summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces seized key positions and large parts of Dhubab district overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to three military sources and one government source cited by Reuters. Houthi-aligned media denied that government forces had advanced. The reported gains followed the government’s October 4 announcement of a nationwide offensive.
candidates.title: Yemeni government forces report gains near Bab el-Mandeb

candidates.summary: Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper said Russian airstrikes targeted industrial and port infrastructure in southern Ukraine and that resulting fires had been extinguished. Russia’s Defense Ministry separately claimed it struck fuel storage facilities and two cargo vessels carrying military equipment or supplies. Those Russian claims were not independently verified in the initial reports.
candidates.title: Russian strikes target Odesa region ports and industry

candidates.summary: Thailand’s Interior Ministry said the death toll from flooding that began September 16 had risen to 31.
candidates.title: Thailand flood death toll rises to 31

candidates.summary: Vaxcyte said its experimental 31-valent pneumococcal vaccine, VAX-31, met all prespecified primary immunogenicity and safety endpoints in a pivotal Phase 3 trial. In adults 50 and older, immune responses met the trial’s noninferiority criterion for all 28 strains shared with at least one comparator vaccine, while three unique strains and cross-reactive strain 20B met a superiority criterion. The results do not constitute regulatory approval; Vaxcyte plans additional trial readouts in 2027 and a U.S. application in 2028.
candidates.title: Vaxcyte pneumococcal vaccine meets Phase 3 trial endpoints

candidates.summary: A Nigerian military aircraft carrying 25 passengers and seven crew members crashed near a naval base in Igbokoda, Ondo state, after air traffic controllers lost contact with it at 08:13 GMT, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said. Authorities located the wreckage and began search-and-rescue operations. No casualties had been confirmed in the initial reports.
candidates.title: Nigerian military aircraft crashes with 32 aboard

candidates.summary: Romanian authorities said two people died and 11 crew members were rescued after the Royad Mammadov caught fire and sank in the Black Sea outside Romania’s territorial waters. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attributed the incident to two Russian drones striking the Turkish-owned civilian grain vessel; Romania did not confirm the cause, and Russia had not commented directly. Russia’s Defense Ministry had separately said it struck two cargo vessels.
candidates.title: Two die after cargo ship burns and sinks in Black Sea

candidates.summary: A humanitarian bulletin circulated among aid groups said overnight airstrikes killed at least 17 people in Adwa and Sheraro in Ethiopia’s Tigray region. It also reported heavy artillery exchanges between federal and Tigrayan forces near the Tekeze River on Monday morning. The bulletin did not identify who conducted the airstrikes, and Reuters said it could not independently verify the casualty reports.
candidates.title: Aid sources report 17 killed in Tigray airstrikes

candidates.summary: A 15-year-old lost a hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police stun grenade during clashes between school protesters and riot police in Lens, according to regional newspaper La Voix du Nord. A local official declined to confirm the precise circumstances. French authorities said 400 to 500 high schools were closed or partly closed amid nationwide protests over school conditions, and reported clashes in several cities.
candidates.title: Teenager severely injured during French school protests

candidates.summary: Russian authorities said contacts of a 28-year-old laboratory worker at an anti-plague research institute in Siberia had been quarantined or placed under medical supervision after she died from pneumonia of unknown origin. Health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said it found no evidence of a pathogen-handling accident, while regional officials said no additional cases had been identified and there was no evidence linking the death to her work.
candidates.title: Russia quarantines contacts after anti-plague institute worker dies

candidates.summary: Yemen’s information minister told Reuters that Saudi-backed government forces had secured effective control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait after taking key positions and the Dhubab airstrip, though another government source said fighting continued near the strait. The Houthis denied government gains. Government military sources separately reported Houthi advances near Taiz, while another government source disputed that a key road had been cut. The UN migration agency said about 184,000 people had been displaced since fighting resumed.
candidates.title: Yemeni government claims effective control of Bab el-Mandeb

candidates.summary: Ukrainian officials said three Russian bombs struck separate parts of Kharkiv, killing six people and injuring 59, including three children. Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said 30 people were hospitalized and three were in serious condition. Residential buildings and warehouses were damaged. Officials separately reported one person killed in Sloviansk and three people injured when a drone struck an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia.
candidates.title: Russian bombing kills six and injures 59 in Kharkiv

candidates.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court heard arguments over whether federal law prevents Boulder, Colorado, from pursuing state-law claims against ExxonMobil and Suncor for alleged climate-related costs and deceptive marketing. Several justices questioned the potential scope of similar litigation and whether the court has jurisdiction at this stage. Justice Samuel Alito recused himself; a 4-4 split would leave intact the Colorado Supreme Court decision allowing the case to proceed. No ruling was issued.
candidates.title: US Supreme Court hears Boulder climate lawsuit dispute
